# The sanitizers of the built-in model, each read once (internal/model/builtin, TestSanitizersAreReviewed).
# One symbol per line, then the kind, then `sha256:` and a hash of what its rows say (drops, adds, flows, match,
# max_implementations, allow_sanitizer_expansion: not the provenance), then a comment after `#`. A change of a row
# fails the test with the new hash: read the change, and write it here.
#   function      a function of a package, never reached through an interface or a trait
#   static        a static method of a class (Dart): never dispatched
#   class-method  an instance method of a concrete class that a subclass may override
#   interface     a method of an interface or a trait (none is written yet)
# A sanitizer says only that its result is clean. The implementations of the project that a call
# through such a symbol may reach are read, with their result dropped (ADR-086): a `class-method` or an
# `interface` row is therefore safe, and listed because it is where that rule is used.
html.EscapeString function sha256:f182ff4ae56e1fc4 # xss
html/template.HTMLEscapeString function sha256:9b041875f10ad776 # xss
html/template.JSEscapeString function sha256:ac62a93ced380006 # xss: a known over-claim, it is for a JavaScript string only (an attribute or a URL needs more)
dart:core#Uri.encodeComponent static sha256:9897afd4b6236737 # neutralises nothing: it keeps ' .. and $(), and where the value lands (host, path, query) decides, so no category is claimed
dart:core#Uri.encodeQueryComponent static sha256:98e1acaaed0f487d # neutralises nothing: same as encodeComponent
dart:convert#HtmlEscape.convert class-method sha256:2d365b8340697c06 # xss; a subclass of HtmlEscape may override convert
